Nicknamed 'the Flautist' for his love of playing the flute at Dionysian festivals, this Macedonian-Greek king ruled Egypt twice and was a descendant of one of Alexander the Great's generals — who was he?
Ptolemy XII Auletes: Ptolemaic King of Egypt, 80–51 BC.
Taking office in December 1983, this Argentine lawyer and social democrat was the first democratically elected president after the country's military 'National Reorganization Process' — who was he?
Raúl Alfonsín: President of Argentina from 1983 to 1989.
Deposed in a 2017 coup after ruling Zimbabwe for 37 years as both prime minister and president, who was this revolutionary-turned-leader?
Robert Mugabe: Leader of Zimbabwe from 1980 to 2017.
In 2023 this German politician walked out of The Left to found a Eurosceptic populist party bearing her own name — which firebrand was she?

Depicted in reliefs at Ramesses III's mortuary temple, this mysterious maritime confederation was long blamed for Late Bronze Age raids on Egypt around 1200 BC, though scholars now see them more as a symptom of the era's collapse than its cause. Who were they?
Sea Peoples: Purported ancient tribal confederation of the Late Bronze Age.
Serving five separate terms as prime minister between 1995 and 2022, this long-time Nepali Congress leader saw his tenure dogged by accusations of nepotism and corruption — who is he?
Founded in Japan in 1930 and rooted in the teachings of the 13th-century monk Nichiren, this Buddhist organization centers its practice on chanting a specific mantra — what is it?
Soka Gakkai: Japanese Buddhist religious movement.
He founded a Korean new religious movement known for mass 'Blessing' wedding ceremonies, and also launched an international news company behind The Washington Times — who was this messiah claimant?
Sun Myung Moon: Korean religious leader (1920–2012)
This Aztec god of the night sky, hurricanes, and conflict had the jaguar as his animal double, and his main festival involved ritual human sacrifice — who is he?
Tezcatlipoca: Aztec deity of darkness and violence.
A vocal champion of the crypto industry in Congress, this Minnesota Republican has served as House majority whip since 2023 after narrowly losing a gubernatorial bid in 2010. Who is he?
Symbolizing both a diamond's indestructibility and a thunderbolt's force, this ritual scepter-like tool is used alongside a bell in Tibetan Buddhist ceremonies — what is it called?
Vajra: Spiritual weapon or symbol in Dharmic religions.
As the 10th Chairman of Russia's State Duma since 2016, this former deputy prime minister and ex-aide to Vladimir Putin is credited with engineering Putin's conservative turn — who is he?

Convicted by court-martial for his role in the 1968 My Lai massacre during the Vietnam War, this officer ultimately served only three years of house arrest after his sentence was repeatedly reduced — who was he?
William Calley: US Army officer convicted for massacre at My Lai, Vietnam (1943–2024)
Resigning from Japan's Liberal Democratic Party after a 2024 indictment tied to a political slush-fund scandal, this lawmaker had served in the House of Representatives since 2003 — who is he?

Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four. Originally specified in the late 1950s, it is the second-oldest high-level programming language still in common use, after Fortran.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
SQL (founded 1974) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as an astronomer?
Edwin Hubble is an astronomer. Edwin Powell Hubble (November 20, 1889 – September 28, 1953) was an American astronomer.
Which of these four is a mathematician?
Isaac Newton is a mathematician. Newton contributed to and refined the scientific method, and his work is considered the most influential in bringing forth modern science.
What is the atomic number of Caesium?
Caesium (IUPAC spelling; also spelled cesium in American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Cs and atomic number 55.
What is the atomic number of Tungsten?
Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
In what year was Saint Valentine born?
Saint Valentine was a clergyman – either a priest or a bishop – in the Roman Empire who ministered to persecuted Christians.
In what year was Doc Holliday born?
Doc Holliday: Holliday is best known for his role in the events surrounding and his participation in the gunfight at the O.K.
In what year was Johannes Kepler born?
Johannes Kepler (27 December 1571 – 15 November 1630) was a German polymath who was an astronomer, mathematician, astrologer, natural philosopher and music theorist.
In what year did William James Sidis die?
William James Sidis: Born to Boris Sidis, a prominent psychiatrist, and Sarah Mandelbaum Sidis, a physician, Sidis demonstrated extraordinary intellectual capabilities from infancy.
In what year did Thomas Edison die?
Thomas Edison: Thomas Alva Edison (February 11, 1847 – October 18, 1931) was an American inventor and businessman.
In what year was Helium discovered?
Helium: Helium (from Ancient Greek: ἥλιος, romanized: helios, lit. 'sun') is a chemical element; it has symbol He and atomic number 2.
Mil Mi-24: Mil Moscow Helicopter Plant. It is produced by Mil Moscow Helicopter Plant and was introduced by the Soviet Air Force in 1972.
Which country is General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon from?
General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon: United States. The aircraft was first developed by General Dynamics in 1974.
HTML: United Kingdom. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
Who is credited with discovering Moscovium?
Moscovium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
Who is credited with discovering Oxycodone?
Oxycodone: Martin Freund. It is a highly addictive and commonly abused drug.
Who is credited with discovering Germanium?
Germanium: Clemens Winkler. Germanium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ge and atomic number 32.
Heading Switzerland's Federal Department of Home Affairs for over a decade, this politician succeeded Marija Pejčinović Burić atop a major European institution in 2024 — who is he?
Alain Berset (French; born 9 April 1972) is a Swiss politician who served as a Member of the Swiss Federal Council from 2012 to 2023.
With a wingspan up to 3.3 meters and a weight of 15 kilograms, which South American bird is generally considered the largest bird of prey on Earth, sporting a ruff of white feathers around its neck?
Andean condor (Vultur gryphus) is a South American New World vulture and is the only extant member of the genus Vultur.
Native to Europe and Asia, which genus of burdock plants owes its seed-dispersal success to burrs that later inspired a famous fastening invention?
Arctium is a genus of biennial plants commonly known as burdock, family Asteraceae.
This American physicist shared the 2017 Nobel with Rainer Weiss and Kip Thorne for decisive contributions to LIGO and the observation of gravitational waves — who is he?
Barry Barish (born January 27, 1936) is an American experimental physicist and Nobel Laureate.
So dense that not even light can escape its gravity, this astronomical object's boundary of no return is called the event horizon — name it?
Black hole is an astronomical body so compact that its gravity prevents anything, including light, from escaping.
Splitting from the windpipe at the carina into a right and left branch, this airway keeps forking into ever-smaller tubes until it's too narrow for cartilage support — what is it?
Bronchus (pl.: bronchi) is a passage or airway in the lower respiratory tract that conducts air into the lungs.
Also called meridian fennel, this biennial plant in the carrot family is native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa — name it?
Caraway (Carum carvi), also known as meridian fennel, is a biennial plant in the family Apiaceae, native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa.
Her famous experiment proved that parity is not conserved — yet the 1957 Nobel went to two male colleagues while she earned the first-ever Wolf Prize in Physics. Which Manhattan Project physicist?

Chien-Shiung Wu (pinyin: W Jinxing; May 31, 1912 - February 16, 1997) was a Chinese-American particle and experimental physicist who made significant contributions in the fields of nuclear and particle physics.

Native to tropical Africa and Asia, this genus of flowering shrubs and small trees in the Rubiaceae family produces caffeine-rich seeds that are roasted and ground into a beloved beverage worldwide — which genus?
Coffea is a genus of flowering plants in the family Rubiaceae. The seeds of some species, called coffee beans, are roasted and ground to brew into various coffee beverages.
Affecting roughly 1 in 22,000 births and more common in girls, which genetic condition caused by a chromosome 5 deletion takes its French name from a feline-sounding cry?
Cri du chat syndrome is a rare genetic disorder due to a partial chromosome deletion on chromosome 5.
With interlocking neck vertebrae that prevent almost any head movement, which genus of prehensile-tailed marsupials is commonly called the large American opossums?
Didelphis is a genus of New World marsupials.
This English physician created the world's first vaccine, targeting smallpox, and in doing so coined the very term 'vaccine' — derived from the Latin for 'pustules of the cow.' Who was he?
Edward Jenner (17 May 1749 - 26 January 1823) was an English physician and scientist who pioneered the concept of vaccines and created the smallpox vaccine, the world's first vaccine.
This class of mental health condition is defined by an enduring, pervasive pattern of behavior, emotion, and thought that deviates from social norms and develops early in life. What is it?
Erythritol is an organic compound, the naturally occurring achiral meso four-carbon sugar alcohol (or polyol).
This body part is a prominent, usually flexible digit found on the forelimbs of most four-limbed vertebrates — on the hind limbs, the equivalent shorter digits are instead called toes. What is it?
Finger is a prominent digit on the forelimbs of most tetrapod vertebrate animals, especially those with prehensile extremities (i.e.

Cataloged by the astronomer Ptolemy in the second century AD and still one of the 88 modern constellations, this zodiac constellation takes its Latin name from the mythological twins Castor and Pollux — what's the constellation?
Gemini (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the northern celestial hemisphere.
Bred for centuries to hunt by sight and speed rather than scent, this ancient dog breed's deep chest, flexible spine, and long legs make it one of the fastest breeds alive. Name the breed?
Greyhound is a breed of dog and a sighthound. It is an ancient breed historically developed for hunting game by sight and speed, and has later been used in organised coursing and greyhound racing.

This field of study concerns the methodological principles of interpretation — especially of biblical, philosophical, and wisdom texts — and has been broadly applied across law, history, and theology — what's it called?

Hermeneutics is the study of the methodological principles of interpretation, especially the interpretation of biblical texts, wisdom literature, and philosophical texts. As necessary, hermeneutics may include the art of understanding and communication.
Related to the sodium and calcium compounds found in household bleach, this chlorine-based oxidizer also occurs naturally as part of the human immune system. What is it?
Hypochlorous acid is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula ClOH, also written as HClO, HOCl, or ClHO.
Eaten raw or turned into jams and wine, this round Brazilian fruit is famous for growing directly on the trunk of its own tree — what is it?
Jabuticaba is a round, edible fruit produced by a jaboticaba tree (Plinia cauliflora), also known as Brazilian grapetree.

After leaving the company where he led industrial design for decades, this British-American designer founded the creative collective LoveFrom, which now works with Ferrari, Airbnb, and OpenAI. Who is he?
Jony Ive (born 27 February 1967) is a British-American designer.
Originally a water-retrieving gun dog from Italy's Po Delta marshes, this breed later became prized for hunting truffles once its wetland habitat was drained — what breed is it?
Lagotto Romagnolo is an Italian breed of dog.
This common, soft, movable, painless growth made of fatty tissue usually forms just under the skin, often on the back, shoulders, or abdomen — name this benign tumor?
Lipoma is a benign tumor made of fat tissue. The first use of the term "lipoma" to describe these tumors was in 1709.

Located partly outside the body and partly within the pelvis, this set of sex organs includes the testicles, which produce sperm to fertilize an egg during conception — which body system is being described?
Male reproductive system consists of a number of sex organs that play a role in the process of human reproduction.
Triggered by falling progesterone, this monthly discharge from the uterine lining signals that pregnancy hasn't occurred and typically first arrives at "menarche" between ages 11 and 13 — what is it?
Menstruation (also known as a period, among other colloquial terms) is the regular discharge of blood and mucosal tissue from the inner lining of the uterus through the vagina.
Named from a Greek word for lead because its ores were once confused with lead ore, this chemical element bears the symbol Mo and atomic number 42 — name the element?
Molybdenum is a chemical element; it has symbol Mo and atomic number 42.

What term, coined in the mid-19th century and often attributed to pathologist Rudolf Virchow, describes the premature death of cells in living tissue due to external injury or infection, as opposed to programmed cell death?
Necrosis (from Ancient Greek (nkrsis) 'death') is a form of cell injury which results in the premature death of cells in living tissue by autolysis.
This insect order includes dragonflies and damselflies, the bulkier ones holding wings out at rest while the slender ones fold theirs along the body — what is it?
Odonata is an order of predatory flying insects that includes the dragonflies and damselflies (as well as the Epiophlebia damsel-dragonflies).
Contrasted with 'normophilic' interests and famously tallied at up to 549 types by Anil Aggrawal, this contested clinical category covers atypical sexual attraction — what's its name?
Paraphilia is an uncommon, intense, and persistent sexual arousal or attraction to anything not sexual by nature, though preference is favored for specific designations.

This cellular process, in which a cell's outer membrane engulfs a large particle to form an internal compartment, is a key immune-system mechanism for clearing pathogens and cellular debris — what is it called?

Phagocytosis (from Ancient Greek (phagein) 'to eat' and (kytos) 'cell') is the process by which a cell uses its plasma membrane to engulf a large particle (0.5 m), giving rise to an internal compartment called the phagosome.
Carrying minor-planet number 134340, this icy Kuiper-belt world has about one-sixth the Moon's mass and got demoted when astronomers rewrote the rules — what is it?
Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Unfolding inside every cell in two acts called transcription and translation, this process turns a gene's DNA into messenger RNA on its way to building enzymes and hormones — what is it?
Protein biosynthesis is a core biological process, occurring inside cells, balancing the loss of cellular proteins (via degradation or export) through the production of fresh proteins.

This bird of prey now breeds only in Europe, though it once also ranged across West Asia and Northwest Africa, with northern populations historically wintering as far as western Africa — what bird is it?
Red kite (Milvus milvus) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as eagles, buzzards, and harriers.
This root vegetable — a hybrid of cabbage and a related turnip-like plant — goes by different names in North America and Britain, and is often confused for a big turnip. What is it?
Rutabaga (North American English) or swede (British English and some Commonwealth English) is a root vegetable, a form of Brassica napus (which also includes rapeseed).
This interdisciplinary field studies signs and sign systems, breaking down into branches examining the formal relations between signs, their meanings, and their users — what's the field called?
Semiotics is the study of signs. It is an interdisciplinary field that examines what signs are, how they form sign systems, and how individuals use them to communicate meaning.
A white crystalline compound most important industrially as a nitrite salt, and probably best known as a food additive in processed meats. What is it?
Sodium nitrite is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula NaNO2.

This alkaline earth metal, symbol Sr and atomic number 38, shares chemical properties with its periodic-table neighbors calcium and barium, and is mostly mined from the minerals celestine and strontianite — what element is it?
Strontium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sr and atomic number 38. The metal forms a dark oxide layer when it is exposed to air.
Named for a U.S. state where its discovery research was based, this synthetic element (symbol Ts) holds the second-highest atomic number of all and was the most recently discovered — what is it?
Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.
Divided into the thorax, abdomen, and pelvis, this core section of the body is where the head, neck, and all four limbs attach — which body part?
Torso is the central part, or the core, of the body of many animals (including human beings), from which the head, neck, limbs, tail and other appendages extend.
As head of the WWII Office of Scientific Research and Development, this MIT engineer steered nearly all American military R&D, including radar and the early Manhattan Project — who was he?
Vannevar Bush (van-; March 11, 1890 - June 28, 1974) was an American engineer, inventor and science administrator, who during World War II headed the U.S.
This Austrian physicist earned a 1945 Nobel Prize for the exclusion principle and, in 1930, proposed the existence of what would become known as the neutrino — who is he?
Wolfgang Pauli (25 April 1900 - 15 December 1958) was an Austrian theoretical physicist and a pioneer of quantum mechanics.
This bird-of-prey family boasts 256 species including eagles, hawks, kites, and harriers, though the osprey and secretary bird are classified separately — which family is it?
Accipitridae: Family of birds of prey. The Accipitridae have a cosmopolitan distribution, being found on all the world's continents (except Antarctica) and a number of oceanic island groups.
Conceived as a clean-sheet 'extra wide body' answer to Boeing's Dreamliner, this twin-engine jet first lifted off from Toulouse in 2013 on Rolls-Royce Trent power — which airliner is it?
Airbus A350: Large twin-aisle airliner family.
Refined from bauxite and nicknamed alumina, this compound shows up in nature as the mineral corundum — the very stuff of rubies and sapphires. What is it?
Aluminium oxide: Chemical compound. Aluminium oxide (or aluminium(III) oxide) is a chemical compound of aluminium and oxygen with the chemical formula Al2O3.
Named for a modified fin ray it dangles like bait to lure in prey, this order of mostly bottom-dwelling creatures is known for extreme sexual dimorphism between the sexes — what are they called?
Anglerfish: Bony fish with a natural lure.

Once mistaken for bacteria, this domain of single-celled organisms is now known to be the group from which eukaryotes evolved, distinguished by ether-linked cell membranes and a unique whip-like motility structure. What domain is it?
Archaea: Domain of organisms. Traditionally, Archaea included only its prokaryotic members, but has since been found to be paraphyletic, as eukaryotes are known to have evolved from archaea.
Sold under the brand name Strattera, this selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor treats ADHD and is only recommended for patients age six and up — what is this medication?
Atomoxetine: Medication used to treat ADHD.
Second only to the capybara among living rodents and able to top 50 kg, this animal sports chisel-like incisors, webbed back feet, and a flat, scaly tail — what is it?
This portmanteau of 'binary digit' is the most basic unit of information in computing, representing one of two possible states like 0 or 1 — eight of them make up a byte. What is it?
Bit: Unit of information. The bit represents a logical state with one of two possible values.

Unlike most elements, this one is forged entirely by cosmic-ray spallation and supernovae rather than stellar fusion, and is mined from evaporite minerals like borax, mostly in Turkey — which element?
Boron: Chemical element with atomic number 5 (B)
Encompassing reporting, dashboards, data mining, and analytics, this set of strategies and technologies helps companies turn raw data into strategic decisions — what's it called?
Business intelligence: Strategies for analysis and use of data.
Domesticated in Mexico roughly 6,000 years ago, this nightshade produces berries used in cooking, medicine, and even self-defense sprays — which plant species is it?
Capsicum annuum: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family.
Originally called 'centigrade' from Latin words for a hundred and steps, this SI temperature scale was renamed in 1948 to honor the Swedish astronomer who proposed it in 1742 — which scale?
Celsius: Unit of measurement for temperature.
Once common as the refrigerant "Freon," these carbon-chlorine-fluorine compounds were phased out under the Montreal Protocol for chewing through the ozone layer — what are they?
Home to jellyfish, corals, and sea anemones, this phylum of aquatic invertebrates is defined by specialized stinging cells used to capture prey — what is it?
Cnidaria: Aquatic animal phylum having cnidocytes.

This physician was convicted of involuntary manslaughter in 2011 after inadvertently overdosing his famous patient with the anesthetic propofol, which he had been improperly using as a sleep aid — who is he?
Conrad Murray: American physician and convicted felon (born 1953)
Encompassing roadrunners, koels, and anis among its roughly 150 species, this widespread bird family favors trees but includes some ground-dwellers — what is it?
Cuckoo: Family of birds. The cuckoo family includes the common or European cuckoo, roadrunners, koels, malkohas, couas, coucals, and anis.
This biological process, powered by rhythmic muscle waves called peristalsis, expels solid waste from the digestive tract through the anus or cloaca — what is it?
Defecation: Expulsion of feces from the digestive tract.
A dentist and gambler who fought alongside lawman Wyatt Earp at the O.K. Corral, his reputation claimed dozens of killings though researchers count just one to three — who was this gunfighter?
Doc Holliday: Gambler, gunfighter, and dentist in the American West (1851–1887)
Now the wealthiest Brazilian and the richest person in Singapore, this Facebook co-founder later started the venture firm B Capital — who is he?
Coiled to just 6 to 7 centimetres but stretching nearly 20 feet if unraveled, this tube connects each testicle to the vas deferens and stores maturing sperm — what is it?

Epididymis: Tube that connects a testicle to a vas deferens. The epididymis serves as an interconnection between the multiple efferent ducts at the rear of a testicle (proximally), and the vas deferens (distally).
The most widely distributed member of its subfamily, this semiaquatic, fish-eating mustelid ranges across Europe, much of Asia, and North Africa's Maghreb — which animal?
Discovered in the fallout debris of the first hydrogen bomb test in 1952 and named for a pioneer of nuclear physics, this element 100 is the heaviest you can make by neutron bombardment. What is it?
Fermium: Chemical element with atomic number 100 (Fm)
This American physician-scientist led the Human Genome Project before directing the NIH for over a decade under three presidents — who guided the mapping of our DNA?

Named after a long-nosed, insect-eating African animal, this 1960s supersonic fighter-bomber pioneered variable-sweep wings and automated terrain-following radar under Robert McNamara's TFX program. What aircraft is it?
General Dynamics F-111 Aardvark: Family of strike aircraft developed in 1960s.
Caused by iodine deficiency in over 90% of cases worldwide, this neck swelling results from an enlarged thyroid gland — what's the condition called?
Goitre: Neck swelling due to enlarged thyroid gland. A goitre (British English, spelled goiter in American English) is a swelling in the neck resulting from an enlarged thyroid gland.

Named from Greek words meaning 'naked seed,' this group of woody plants — including conifers, cycads, and ginkgos — lacks the protective covering that encloses a flowering plant's seeds. What is it called?
Gymnosperm: Clade of non-flowering, naked-seeded vascular plants.
This Dutch-born entrepreneur produced Japan's first major turn-based role-playing game and later secured the console distribution rights to a Russian puzzle game called Tetris — who is he?
Henk Rogers: Dutch-born American computer programmer (born 1953)
Despite the name, this 'living fossil' is no crustacean at all — it's a chelicerate, kin to spiders and scorpions, and its three-part body ends in a spiky tail called a telson. What creature is it?
Horseshoe crab: Family of basal chelicerates.
This mammal order today includes only small African and Middle Eastern hyraxes, but once boasted a species weighing up to 600 kilograms called Titanohyrax — which order?
Hyracoidea: Order of mammals. It includes the living hyraxes, placed within the family Procaviidae, and several extinct taxa.
She and her husband won the 1935 Nobel in Chemistry for discovering induced radioactivity — making her half of the only mother-daughter pair to both win Nobel Prizes. Who is this scientist?
Irène Joliot-Curie: French chemist and physicist (1897–1956)

This temporary condition throws your internal body clock out of sync with local time after rapid travel across multiple time zones — and most people find it harder to shake off flying east than west — what is it?

Jet lag: Condition due to travel across time zones. The phase shift when travelling from east to west is referred to as phase-delay of the circadian cycle, whereas going west to east is phase-advance of the cycle.

Known to NATO by the reporting name Hokum A and nicknamed 'Black Shark' for its distinctive coaxial rotors, this Russian single-seat attack helicopter has a rare rescue ejection system — which aircraft?
Kamov Ka-50: Attack helicopter. It was designed in the 1980s and adopted for service in the Russian army in 1995.
With a toothed, funnel-like sucking mouth, this jawless fish's name may derive from Latin for 'stone licker,' and it's genetically closer to hagfish than to any jawed vertebrate — what is it?
Lamprey: Class of jawless fish. Lampreys (sometimes inaccurately called lamprey eels) are a group of jawless fish composing the order Petromyzontiformes, sole order in the class Petromyzontida.
As a principal shareholder of L'Oréal, this French heiress was the richest woman in the world at the time of her death in 2017, worth $44.3 billion — who was she?
Liliane Bettencourt: French heiress, socialite and businesswoman (1922–2017)
Native to Africa except for one species found only on Madagascar, this small parrot gets its common name from its strong, monogamous pair-bonding behavior — what is it?
Oblate rather than round, with a thin, loose peel that makes it easy to separate into segments, this citrus fruit is sweeter and stronger-tasting than its spherical, hybrid cousin — which fruit?
Mandarin orange: Small citrus fruit. A mandarin orange (Citrus reticulata), often simply called mandarin, is a small, rounded citrus tree fruit.
This small, highly social mongoose from southern Africa lives in packs of up to 30, with a dominance hierarchy where usually only the top pair breeds. What animal is it?
Meerkat: Species of mongoose from Southern Africa. The meerkat (Suricata suricatta) or suricate is a small mongoose found in southern Africa.
This scientific field studies microorganisms such as bacteria, fungi, and protists, encompassing sub-disciplines like virology and mycology — which discipline?

Thought to enjoy 'hybrid vigor' and a reduced risk of inbreeding-linked health problems, this catch-all term covers roughly 150 million dogs worldwide that don't belong to any officially recognized breed — what's it called?
This arthropod subphylum includes millipedes and centipedes, and one of its earliest fossils preserves the first known evidence of animals breathing air on land. What's the group called?
Myriapoda: Subphylum of arthropods. The group contains about 13,000 species, all of them terrestrial.
This Serbian-American engineer designed the modern alternating current electricity supply system—the backbone of today's power grid. Who?
Nikola Tesla: Serbian-American engineer and inventor (1856–1943)
Sold under the brand name Zyprexa, this atypical antipsychotic treats schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, and is sometimes used off-label to fight chemotherapy-induced nausea — what is this drug?
Olanzapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Olanzapine, sold under the brand name Zyprexa among others, is an atypical antipsychotic primarily used to treat schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
Prized both as a delicacy and, in some species, for the pearls grown within its shell, which salt-water bivalve is this?
Oyster: Variety of families of Mollusca.
Carl Linnaeus named this crop 'hypogaea' — Greek for 'under the earth' — because, unlike most legumes, it ripens its pods below ground. What is it?
Peanut: Legume cultivated as a grain and oil crop.
Its name combines the Greek words for 'love' and 'tree,' and with over 600 accepted species it's the second-largest genus in the arum family after Anthurium — which popular houseplant genus?
Caused by viral infections, autoimmune disorders, or pulmonary embolism, this condition inflames the membranes lining the lungs and chest cavity, causing sharp pain when breathing — which condition?
Pleurisy: Disease of the lungs. Pleurisy, also known as pleuritis, is inflammation of the membranes that surround the lungs and line the chest cavity (pleurae).
Caused by a single mutation in the LMNA gene, this rare disorder causes children to age dramatically faster than normal, with most not living past their twenties — which condition?
Progeria: Genetic disorder that causes early aging.
In Euclidean geometry, which fundamental relation says the square on a right triangle's longest side equals the sum of the squares on the other two — famously written a² + b² = c²?
Pythagorean theorem: Relation between sides of a right triangle.
Rooted in Minangkabau cooking at the crossroads of the Malacca Strait, this dish slow-cooks meat in spiced coconut milk until the oil separates and it fries in its own glaze — what is it?

Nicknamed the 'dark lady of DNA,' this X-ray crystallographer's crucial contributions to the discovery of DNA's structure went largely unrecognized in her lifetime — James Watson believed she'd have won a Nobel Prize had she lived. Who was she?
Also called Besnier–Boeck–Schaumann disease, this non-infectious condition forms clusters of inflammatory cells called granulomata, often starting in the lungs, skin, or lymph nodes — what is it?
Sarcoidosis: Abnormal formation of clumps of inflammatory cells (granulomata)
About 90% of this mood-regulating neurotransmitter is actually made in your gut, where it controls intestinal movement, rather than the brain — also known as 5-HT, what is it?
Serotonin: Monoamine neurotransmitter. It is involved in mood, cognition, reward, learning, memory, and physiological processes such as vomiting and vasoconstriction.
Coined in the late 18th century, this social science studies human society — from one-on-one interactions to sweeping social structures and everyday culture. What is it?
Sociology: Scientific study of human society and relationships.

Developed in 1962 by an American pharmaceutical company and derived from a natural male hormone, this anabolic steroid treats hereditary angioedema and is unusual for surviving liver metabolism without being esterified — what is it?
Stanozolol: Discontinued steroid for heart treatment.

Blending geodesy, trigonometry, and law, this profession uses tools like theodolites, GNSS receivers, and lidar scanners to fix the exact positions of points on Earth for maps and property boundaries — what is it?
Surveying: Science of determining the positions of points and the distances and angles between them.
